# 7th Kalasha International Film & TV Awards

The 7th Kalasha International Film & TV Awards ceremony, presented by the Kenya Film Commission, honoured the best in Kenyan television and film for the year 2017. It took place on 9 December 2017 at the Crowne Plaza in Nairobi, Kenya. The awards recognize excellence in storytelling, direction, performance and technical execution in the Kenyan entertainment industry.
Mbithi Masya's critically acclaimed film Kati Kati dominated the ceremony, sweeping six major awards, including Best Feature Film, Best Director and multiple technical categories. In the television categories, the comedy-drama Sue na Jonnie took top honours, winning Best TV Drama, as well as both Best Lead Actor and Best Lead Actress for Martin Githinji and Catherine Kamau, respectively.
Ceremony
The 7th edition of the awards ceremony was held on 9 December 2017 at the Crowne Plaza in Nairobi. The 2017 edition marked a significant milestone for the Kenya Film Commission, registering 237 film submissions—the highest number of films ever submitted since the awards' inception.
To accommodate this growth, the Kalasha International event was split into three distinct segments: the Kalasha International Film Festival (held from 4 to 8 December 2017), the Kalasha Awards gala (held on 9 December 2017) and the Kalasha Market (set for March 2018). The 2017 awards received significant sponsorship support from various organizations, including IMAX Kenya, the Kenya Film Classification Board (KFCB), ADMI Africa, NTV Kenya, Fanaka TV, MTECH, English Press, the Embassy of Argentina and the Communications Authority of Kenya.
